title: Building Materials Requiring Conformity 2026: Homeowner Checks
desc: Which materials need a declaration of conformity under Circular 41/2026/TT-BXD: glass, plasterboard, cement, tiles, paint, pipes, and what to check.
summary: The list of high- and medium-risk building materials that must have a declaration of conformity under Circular 41/2026/TT-BXD, and the documents homeowners should ask suppliers and contractors for.
body: p

From 1 July 2026, the quality of building materials is managed by risk level under Circular 41/2026/TT-BXD (replacing Circular 10/2024/TT-BXD) and Decree 209/2026/ND-CP. Knowing which materials must be conformity-certified helps homeowners avoid buying poor-quality goods.
h2
1. Materials are divided into 3 risk groups
p
Under Article 3 and Article 5 of Circular 41/2026/TT-BXD:
ul
High risk (Appendix II) and medium risk (Appendix III): a declaration of conformity is mandatory against the corresponding technical regulation, with labeling before sale.
Low risk (all other materials): a quality management system under the declared standard and labeling apply; a declaration of standard conformity is voluntary.
h2
2. Commonly used housing materials that must be conformity-certified
p
Under Appendices II and III attached to Circular 41/2026/TT-BXD:
ul

High-risk group: building glass (float glass, reflective coated glass, Low-E glass, tempered glass, multi-layer safety laminated glass, insulating glass units); plasterboard and fiber-reinforced gypsum panels; fly ash and granulated slag for concrete and cement; white asbestos.

Medium-risk group: Portland cement, blended Portland cement, sulfate-resistant cement; emulsion wall paint; PE, PP, and PVC pipes and fittings for pressurized water supply and drainage; engineered wood panels; paving and cladding stone; ceramic tiles; autoclaved aerated concrete products; wall panels; roofing tiles; sanitary ware (washbasins, urinals, floor-mounted toilets).
p
Sand, crushed stone, fired clay bricks, and the like are not in these two appendices and so fall in the low-risk group.
h2
3. On what basis is conformity declared?
p

Under Article 12: the high-risk group declares conformity based on certification results from a certification body designated by the Ministry of Construction; the medium-risk group, based on certification by an accredited or designated body, or on self-assessment using test results from an accredited or designated laboratory. Goods sold on e-commerce platforms in these two groups must publicly post images of the label and the conformity mark (Clause 2, Article 4).
h2
4. Responsibilities of suppliers and contractors
ul

The supplier must test and check quality and provide certificates, certifications, and related documents to the buyer; and repair or replace non-conforming products under its warranty commitment (Clause 1, Article 14 of Decree 207/2026/ND-CP).
Materials must be accepted by the investor's supervisor before being used in the works, with a record (Clause 6, Article 14).
A change in the type or origin of materials must meet the design and be approved by the investor (Clause 8, Article 14).

The contractor is responsible for the quality and origin of materials it supplies and must compensate if it uses the wrong type of material (Points e and k, Clause 2, Article 61 of the Construction Law 2025).
h2
5. What documents should homeowners ask for?
ol
State the type, specifications, and manufacturer of the main materials clearly in the contract.
The manufacturer's quality certificate; and a certificate of conformity for materials in Appendices II and III (Clause 7, Article 14).
Check the product label and the conformity mark on the product and its packaging.
Material test results during construction (if the design requires them) and material acceptance records.
p
Keep these documents with the building file for use in warranty and repair. See also Conditions for starting construction of a house 2026.
note

This article is a summary for reference only and does not replace legal documents. For products in Appendices II and III that do not yet have a corresponding technical regulation, conformity is declared once the regulation is issued; conformity certificates under QCVN 16:2023/BXD issued before 1 July 2026 remain usable while valid (Article 17). Referenced documents such as Decree 37/2026/ND-CP and Circular 14/2026/TT-BKHCN are not yet in our library.
